newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom, Bonn agree share sale.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom, Bonn agree share sale.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG, the German telecoms giant, said on Thursday it has reached an agreement with the government allowing Bonn to sell some of its remaining shares to boost its bid for European monetary union.

The government will transfer 25 percent of its total capital in Telekom to the state development agency Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW) in two steps in 1997 and 1998. The shares will be sold to strategic investors and none of the remaining stock will be sold on capital markets before 2000.

"In this way the government will dispose of its majority stake in Deutsche Telekom sooner than planned, increasing the company's flexibility in order to develop into a global player on the world market," Telekom chairman Ron Sommer said in a regulatory statement.

The deal allows Telekom to search for strategic investors for some of the shares the government plans to sell and the company said it was satisfied that the deal was in the best interests of all of its shareholders.
"As strategic investors, we are looking at current and future partners in the international telecommunications business," Sommer said.

In the run up to Deutsche Telekom's partial privatisation last year, the German government indicated that it would not dispose of its shares before the year 2000. The law privatising Telekom states that none of the shares can be sold directly on the market before then, but allows for a private placement.

But with Bonn finding it difficult to rein in its deficit in time to qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU), Finance Minister Theo Waigel recently said he intended to step up all privatisations and to dispose of Telekom shares early.

German government coalition sources have said the government could gain as much as 25 billion marks over the next two years from the sale of Telekom shares, but the Telekom statement made no mention of expected revenue from the move.

Telekom said that the government's plan to sell its shares would not affect the company's option to carry out the second half of its approved capital increase, which has a remaining volume of 287 million shares.
